newsitem.title: USA: U.S. police hunting Cunanan storm houseboat in vain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. police hunting Cunanan storm houseboat in vain.

text.p: Police searching for Andrew Cunanan, suspected by the FBI of killing fashion designer Gianni Versace, besieged a houseboat moored on Miami Beach for several hours on Wednesday but eventually left empty-handed.

Dozens of police including heavily armed SWAT assault specialists surrounded the houseboat after its caretaker reported a man resembling Cunanan had fired a shot when he approached the site around 4 p.m. EDT (2000 GMT).
Four hours later, police fired tear gas into the houseboat and then entered the two-storey dwelling.
An initial search proved "negative. In other words there is no one inside," said Miami Beach police spokesman Al Boza.
A more thorough search was under way, he said.
The officers who had entered the houseboat were later seen sauntering nonchalantly from the site. Lights could be seen going on board.
Local television stations had said police believed Cunanan, the subject of an intense nationwide manhunt, could be the man inside the houseboat.
Police did not confirm at any time that Cunanan was suspected to be inside, however, saying they were treating the situation like any other reported burglary and shooting.
The siege sparked a frenzy among local media. Television stations carried live images of the site for several hours, although they respected a police request to delay broadcasting the assault itself.

Traffic chaos ensued when authorities cordoned off streets and the waterway surrounding the houseboat, located about 40 blocks from where Versace was killed on July 15 and less than 20 blocks from the hotel where Cunanan had stayed before the killing.
Local television said the owner of the boat was identified as a German citizen who also owns a gay health club in Las Vegas. Police described Cunanan as a homosexual prostitute.
Local television also quoted a law enforcement source as saying police investigated a tip earlier this week that a man looking like Cunanan might be on the houseboat.
Traffic backed up for miles across bridges linking Miami Beach to mainland Florida. Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Miami coast, is a separate city with its own police force.
Cunanan is wanted for four other murders as well as that of Versace during an alleged cross-country killing spree that began in April.
The incident followed possible sightings of Cunanan as far afield as New Hampshire in the northeast United States, near the Canadian border.
Police in New Hampshire investigated two sightings of a man resembling Cunanan on Wednesday, but the FBI expressed doubt a third sighting in the state was actually the alleged killer.

The FBI said it had received more than 1,000 phone calls from across the country from people claiming to have spotted Cunanan. Florida police said Cunanan is a master of disguise and may be dressed as a woman.
The FBI on Tuesday said a bullet recovered from Versace's body matched the gun used in two of the four other murders of which Cunanan is suspected.
